spec.name: mr1_rev1m_alone
spec._hypothesis: Core claim, unadorned: buy the biggest 1-month losers in the liquid universe and hold 10 sessions. If short-horizon reversal exists at all it should show here. No filters, no second factor - anything positive later must beat this.

spec.name: mr2_rev1w_fast
spec._hypothesis: Reversal decays fast, so test the fastest horizon at its own speed: buy the biggest 1-week losers and hold exactly one rebalance period (5 sessions). Weekly reversal is the Lehmann/Lo-MacKinlay effect; a 10-20 day hold would dilute it.

spec.name: mr3_rev1m_quality
spec._hypothesis: Same signal as mr1, restricted to structurally healthy names: above the 200DMA and annualised vol <= 0.45 (~173 of 289 names pass). Separates 'dip in a good stock' from 'falling knife'. Differs from mr1 by the filter alone, so the comparison is clean.

spec.name: mr4_dip_in_leader
spec._hypothesis: Momentum-conditional reversal, the best-documented form of the anomaly: the stock is a 63-day leader against its own sector and is in a 200DMA uptrend, but has fallen over the last month. Buy that pullback rather than the outright loser. Sector-relative strength also strips out sector-wide drawdowns.

spec.name: mr5_sector_rel_loser
spec._hypothesis: Sector-relative contrarian, the mirror of mr4: fell last month AND has lagged its own sector over 63 days (negative weight on rs_vs_sector). Isolates idiosyncratic losers rather than stocks dragged down with their whole sector - the classic over-reaction candidate. rs_vs_sector has full coverage on the base universe, so the negative weight introduces no NaN bias.

spec.name: mr6_lottery_max
spec._hypothesis: The MAX / lottery-demand effect (Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw): avoid stocks that just printed a large single-day gain, because lottery demand overprices them and it unwinds. A contrarian signal that is only +0.47 rank-correlated with reversal_1m, so it is a genuinely different cut at over-reaction. Its natural horizon is monthly, hence max_hold 20. Vol cap is hygiene only.

spec.name: rb1_sectorlag_only
spec._hypothesis: DECOMPOSITION of mr5. mr5 = reversal_1m + (-rs_vs_sector). mr1 showed the reversal_1m leg alone is ~zero out of sample, so strip it out and run the sector-laggard leg by itself. If this reproduces mr5's out-of-sample edge, mr5 is not a short-horizon reversal result at all - it is a 63-day sector-relative reversal, a different animal.

spec.name: rb2_hold5
spec._hypothesis: HORIZON SENSITIVITY of mr5, shorter. Identical selection, hold 5 sessions instead of 10. A real over-reaction effect should decay smoothly with horizon, not exist only at one hold length.

spec.name: rb3_hold20
spec._hypothesis: HORIZON SENSITIVITY of mr5, longer. Identical selection, hold 20 sessions instead of 10.

spec.name: rb4_topn40
spec._hypothesis: BREADTH SENSITIVITY of mr5. Same selection, 40 picks per scan instead of 20. A real ranking effect should still be present (weaker) at twice the breadth; an edge that lives only in exactly 20 names is small-sample noise.

spec.name: rb5_timeonly
spec._hypothesis: EXIT SENSITIVITY of mr5. Same selection, pure time exit with no stop at all. Isolates whether the measured edge comes from the ranking or from the 2.5-ATR stop's path dependence interacting with beaten-down, high-vol names.

spec.name: rb6_weight_half
spec._hypothesis: WEIGHT SENSITIVITY of mr5. Halve the sector-laggard leg (-0.5 instead of -1.0), tilting the blend back toward plain reversal_1m. Together with rb1 this traces the edge across the full mixing range from pure reversal (mr1) to pure sector-lag (rb1).
